column1: It's not just oil and natural gas production that's booming; we're becoming a global leader in clean energy innovation. Solar panels glisten on rooftops from coast to coast, and wind turbines spin proudly across our heartland. But this progress isn’t just about technology—it’s about people. It’s about the workers who’ve retooled their skills, the entrepreneurs who’ve dared to dream, and the communities that have rallied together to build a brighter, more sustainable future. That’s the American spirit—unyielding, inventive, and always moving forward.

Now, little more than 40 years ago, astronauts descended the nine-rung ladder of the lunar module and stepped onto the surface of the moon, proving that when we unite behind a common purpose, there’s no limit to what we can achieve. That same spirit of exploration and determination lives on in us today. It’s what drives us to tackle the challenges of our time — to heal our planet, to bridge divides, to lift up those who’ve been left behind. Together, we can reach new heights, not just in science and technology, but in how we care for one another, how we build a future that’s fair and just for all. Let’s remember that the moon landing wasn’t just a triumph of engineering; it was a testament to the power of hope, the belief that even the most audacious dreams are within our grasp if we dare to pursue them.

We agree that real opportunity requires every American to get the education and training they need to compete in a 21st-century economy. That’s why we’ve invested in community colleges, expanded access to Pell Grants, and supported apprenticeships that lead to good-paying jobs. But we also know that opportunity isn’t just about skills—it’s about fairness. It’s about ensuring that every worker, no matter their background, has a shot at success. Together, we can build an economy that works for everyone, not just the privileged few.

For we, the people, understand that our country cannot succeed when a shrinking few do very well while an expanding majority barely gets by. We know that our nation thrives when everyone has a fair shot, when hard work is rewarded, and when we lift each other up instead of pushing each other down. That’s the promise of America — not just for some, but for all. It’s about ensuring that every child, in every corner of this country, has the chance to dream big and reach higher. It’s about creating an economy that works for the many, not just the privileged few. And it’s about recognizing that our strength lies in our unity — in our belief that together, we can overcome any challenge and build a brighter future for generations to come.

One senator, as you all are aware, had put a hold on every single nominee for senior positions across the government. Now, I understand that politics can be messy, and disagreements are part of the fabric of our democracy. But when it comes to the basic functions of our government—when it comes to ensuring that critical roles are filled so we can serve the American people—political brinkmanship must not take precedence over progress. It’s not just about one senator or one party; it’s about the millions of families, workers, and communities who depend on us to do our jobs. We owe it to them to rise above the gridlock, to find common ground, and to keep moving this country forward. That’s what they expect, and that’s what they deserve.
